intro.headline: Representation built around the decision, not the transaction.
body: Kaylin Smith is a Broker with RE/MAX Epic Realty Inc., Brokerage, working with buyers, sellers and investors across Markham, Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area.

Most of the consequential decisions in a move are made before anyone books a showing. Budget. Location. Timeline. Whether to buy first or sell first. Those decisions constrain everything after them, and they are where the real work belongs.

contact_cta.headline: Let's talk about your next move.
contact_cta.body: Three weeks or three years from a decision, it is worth talking early.

about.hero_subhead: Real estate decisions deserve more than a transaction. They deserve a strategy.

who_i_am.headline: Real estate decisions deserve more than a transaction.
body: I help first-time homebuyers, investors, homeowners and sellers across Markham, Toronto, Durham Region and the GTA make informed real estate decisions with confidence.
I am a Real Estate Broker with RE/MAX Epic Realty Inc., Brokerage, and an investor with more than a decade of experience in real estate and investing.

My perspective on real estate comes from both sides of the transaction. I am a real estate professional and an investor myself. My first investment property was a condominium in Richmond Hill, purchased in 2006.

Over the years I have developed a broader understanding of the financial, business and strategic considerations that can influence a real estate decision. My background in financial services, business and consulting allows me to look beyond the immediate transaction and help clients understand the numbers, the opportunity, the risks and the bigger picture.
Buying a first home, building an investment portfolio, preparing to sell, working out whether to move at all: the approach is the same.
who_i_am.close: Real estate is one of the biggest financial decisions many people make. You deserve advice that is thoughtful, informed and aligned with where you want to go.

who_i_help.headline: Real estate with a strategy behind it.
who_i_help.lead: I work with clients across Markham, Toronto, Durham Region and the GTA, with a particular focus on first-time homebuyers and real estate investors.

groups.title: First-time homebuyers
body: Your first home is more than a purchase. It can be the foundation of your financial future.
I help first-time buyers understand the process, evaluate properties, understand the market and make decisions with confidence.
The goal is not simply to find a home. It is to make the right move for your circumstances and your future.

groups.title: Investors
body: Real estate investing requires more than finding a property that looks good.
I help investors evaluate opportunities, understand the numbers, consider market conditions and think strategically about how a property fits into their broader goals.
My own experience as a real estate investor allows me to approach these conversations from an investor's perspective as well as a real estate professional's.

groups.title: Sellers
body: Selling is about more than putting a property on the market.
I help sellers develop a strategy around pricing, positioning, marketing, negotiation and market conditions to give their property the strongest possible presentation and representation.
Every property and seller is different, so the strategy should be too.

groups.title: Pre-construction
body: Pre-construction can involve significant financial commitments, timelines and long-term considerations.
I help clients evaluate opportunities, understand the financial considerations and determine whether a project makes sense for their goals before they commit.

approach.headline: Strategy before the transaction.
approach.lead: Great real estate representation starts with understanding the person, not just the property. Before recommending a property or strategy, I want to understand:
questions: What are you trying to accomplish?
What does the market mean for your situation?
What do the numbers actually tell us?
What makes sense for your short and long-term goals?
body: I combine market knowledge, research, investment perspective, financial awareness, negotiation and honest advice to help clients make informed decisions.

I do not believe in a one-size-fits-all approach. I believe in asking the right questions, doing the work behind the scenes and giving clients the information they need to make decisions they feel confident about.
No pressure. No unnecessary hype. No telling you what you want to hear just to get the deal.
approach.close: Clear advice. Strong representation. A strategy built around you.

experience.headline: A broader perspective on real estate.
body: My real estate career is supported by experience in investing, financial services, business development and strategic consulting. That background has shaped the way I approach real estate.
I understand that a real estate decision can affect much more than a transaction. It can impact your finances, investment strategy, business, family and long-term plans.

That experience gives me a broader perspective when working with clients, particularly entrepreneurs, investors and clients whose real estate decisions are connected to larger financial or business goals.
My job is to help you understand the opportunity, navigate the process and make a move that makes sense for you.

final_cta.headline: Ready to make your next real estate move?
final_cta.body: A first home, an investment purchase, a sale, or simply working out what your options are. I am here to help you make sense of the market and determine the right strategy for your goals.

consulting.hero_headline: Strategy for the business, and the room.
consulting.hero_body: A separate practice from the real estate brokerage. Consulting for owner-led businesses on positioning, growth, partnerships and the events that carry them.
intro: Owner-led businesses rarely fail on effort. They stall on positioning, on operations that were never designed, and on decisions the owner is too close to make.

Engagements are scoped to a question and produce something written. Where an event is involved, the person who set the objective stays through delivery, so the brief and the execution do not drift apart.

services.title: Strategic Business Consulting
services.body: Who the business is for, what it competes against in a buyer's mind, and what it should stop doing. Most pricing problems turn out to be positioning problems.

services.title: Business Development
services.body: Where the next customers actually come from, and building a way to reach them that does not depend on the owner's calendar.

services.title: Growth Strategy
services.body: What to scale and what to leave alone. Turning what lives in the owner's head into a process someone else can run.

services.title: Brand Partnerships & Activations
services.body: Finding partners whose audience overlaps yours, building an offer worth saying yes to, and running the activation properly.

services.title: Event Strategy
services.body: What the event is for, what it will cost, and whether the format can carry the gap between the two. Concept, budget, vendors, run of show and the debrief most events skip.

services.title: Speaking
services.body: Panels, workshops and keynotes on real estate, business building and brand. Available for corporate, community and industry events.

services.title: Mentorship
services.body: One to one work with agents and early-stage owners on positioning, pipeline and the habits that compound. Limited by design.

consulting.disclaimer: Consulting provided by Kay Smith Consulting Group is advisory and operational in nature. It is not legal, accounting, tax or financial advice. Engage a lawyer or accountant for matters within their scope. This practice is separate from Kaylin's real estate trading services, which are provided through RE/MAX Epic Realty Inc., Brokerage.

contact.hero_headline: Let's talk about your next move.
contact.hero_body: Two ways in, depending on what you need. Real estate enquiries and consulting enquiries go to different places and are answered separately.
contact.response_note: Enquiries are answered directly by Kaylin.

real_estate.hero_body: Buying, selling and investing across Markham, Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area, through RE/MAX Epic Realty Inc., Brokerage.
intro: The difference between a good outcome and an expensive one is rarely the property. It is whether the decision underneath it was examined before anyone committed.

That is what this practice is built around: research the specific market rather than the regional average, build the comparable set by hand, be direct about what the evidence supports, and negotiate from a position prepared in advance.

services.label: I'm Buying
services.title: Buying
services.lead: Finding the property is only part of buying it well.
services.body: Sourcing, comparable analysis, offer construction and negotiation. Most of the leverage in a purchase is created before terms are ever on the table.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.body: What the move is for, what has to be true for it to be worth doing, and where the flexibility actually sits.

steps.title: Financing readiness
steps.body: Full lender approval rather than pre-qualification. Pre-approval assesses you. Approval assesses the property too, and that is the test that fails unexpectedly.

steps.title: Market analysis
steps.body: Absorption, inventory and pricing behaviour in your specific segment and community, not the regional headline.

steps.title: Sourcing and showings
steps.body: Active listings, plus properties surfaced through the brokerage network before or outside general marketing where they exist.

steps.title: Comparable analysis
steps.body: Before any offer, a hand-built comparable set for that specific property. This is what a number should be defended with.

steps.title: Offer and negotiation
steps.body: Price, deposit, closing date, conditions and irrevocable period considered together, with a walk-away point set in advance.

steps.title: Conditions and closing
steps.body: Financing, inspection and status certificate managed against the calendar. These periods are short and unforgiving.

services.label: I'm Selling
services.title: Selling
services.lead: Most homes get listed. Fewer get positioned.
services.body: A listing publishes a property. A strategy decides who sees it, what they assume before they arrive, and what position you negotiate from when an offer comes.

steps.title: Strategy
steps.body: The real timeline, whether it is fixed, and what the sale has to achieve. Buy first or sell first is decided here.

steps.title: Position
steps.body: Which buyer this property is actually for, and where it sits against the inventory that buyer is comparing it to.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.body: The work that returns more than it costs, and only that work. Larger renovations frequently do not return their cost.

steps.title: Present
steps.body: Photography, video and floor plans to a consistent standard, styled for the buyer identified in positioning.

steps.title: Launch
steps.body: Timed deliberately. New listings get concentrated attention from every buyer already searching that band. That audience does not reassemble.

steps.title: Market
steps.body: MLS, syndication, paid digital, social, agent network and open houses, sequenced rather than fired off at once.

steps.title: Negotiate and close
steps.body: Offers reviewed on all terms. Price, deposit, closing date and the strength of the buyer's financing all affect completion.

services.label: I'm Investing
services.title: Investing
services.lead: A property held as an asset is a different decision from a home.
services.body: Different criteria, different analysis, different risks. Gross yield is the figure most often quoted and the least often useful.

steps.title: Criteria
steps.body: What the portfolio is for, the hold horizon, and whether cash flow or appreciation leads. These conflict more often than people expect.

steps.title: Expense modelling
steps.body: Property tax, landlord insurance, condominium fees and their trajectory, and a genuine capital reserve. Roofs and furnaces have finite lives.

steps.title: Financing structure
steps.body: Two identical properties on different terms are different investments. Principal paydown is not an expense in the way interest is.

steps.title: Tenancy
steps.body: The Residential Tenancies Act governs increases, notice and termination. Any model assuming rent moves freely with the market is wrong for much of the stock.

steps.title: Acquisition
steps.body: Assessing a tenanted property at purchase, and what you inherit along with it.

steps.title: Portfolio review
steps.body: Whether each holding still fits the objective it was bought for, and what to do if it does not.

services.label: Real Estate Strategy
services.title: Real Estate Strategy
services.body: Sometimes the right answer is to wait, or to do something other than what you came in for. A strategy call is where that gets worked out, before anyone is committed.

steps.title: Buy first or sell first
steps.body: This single question changes the risk profile of a move entirely, and it has no universally correct answer.

steps.title: Timing
steps.body: What your timeline is genuinely driven by, and whether that driver is fixed or assumed.

steps.title: Capacity
steps.body: What the move actually requires in cash, and what happens if the two sides do not line up.

steps.title: Options
steps.body: Renovate, hold, sell, or move. Laid out with what each one costs and what it gets you.

steps.title: A written read
steps.body: What the evidence supports, in writing, so the decision does not rest on a conversation you half remember.
